data.tombstone: Landscape after Jing Hao and Guan Tong (仿荊關山水), 1700s. Li Shizhuo (Chinese, c. 1690–1770). Hanging scroll; ink on paper; image: 91 x 40.9 cm (35 13/16 x 16 1/8 in.); overall: 226.7 x 68.6 cm (89 1/4 x 27 in.). The Cleveland Museum of Art, John L. Severance Fund, 1952.588
data.title: Landscape after Jing Hao and Guan Tong

inscriptions.inscription: 荆浩自號洪谷子，乃撰山水訣一卷。嘗誇人曰：吳道子有筆無墨，項容有墨無筆。洪谷故能獨擅操縱，而關仝師之。絢唐末之冠。此臨其佳者而更屛其疵焉。李世倬 [印]卓氏; 穀齋; 蝯詹上_ [印, 右下]几研精嚴見性情
inscriptions.inscription_translation:
Artist's inscription, signature, and 4 seals: 

Jing Hao called himself “Honggu Zi.” He wrote the Secret of Landscape. He once proudly stated: “Wu Daozi may excel in brush but is lacking in ink. Xiang Rong may excel in ink but is deficient in brushwork.” Thus Honggu himself could make claim for being a master of both. As a result, Guan Tong sought him out as a teacher. He truly was the leading figure at the end of the Tang dynasty. Here I intend to seek out the best [of Jing Hao] while shedding his flaws.

Li Shizhuo [3 seals] Zhuo shi; Gu zhai, Yuan zhan shang. [seal, lower right corner] Ji yan jing yan jian xing qing.

inscriptions.inscription: 5 additional seals:  1 of C. C. Wang 王季遷 (1907–2003); 4 unidentified.
